# dsh-subagent-codebuddy
A standalone DeepSeek Harness profile bundle: a one-shot subagent provider that runs each child in t
he local **CodeBuddy CLI** (`codebuddy --acp`), with the child's model pinned by config (default `de
epseek-v4.1-flash`, passed as `--model <id>`). Runs consume the logged-in account's subscription cre
dits, or the API key supplied through `envFile`.
The provider is written against the installed harness's public subagent seam (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-suba
gent` helpers `NO_START_CAPABILITIES`, `settleRunResult`, `subprocessRunHandle`) and ships as a bund
le: `dsh.bundle.patch` inserts the provider row plus a tool row that mounts this package's own `./to
undle.patch` inserts the provider row plus a tool row that mounts this package's own `./tool` entry.
Two model-facing tools are mounted, both this package's rather than the generic `@deepseek-ai/dsh-to
ol-subagent`: `subagent_codebuddy` starts a run and `codebuddy_steer` adds a message to one that is
still running. The generic tool renders a bare `started subagent <id>` and offers no wording knob, s
o the model has no reason to stop looking for the run and reaches for `wait_agent` / `list_agents` —
which only track in-process teammates and continuable local children, and therefore always report "
no subagent running" for an out-of-process one-shot child. This tool drives the identical runtime pa
th (`ctx.subagents.startActivation({ delivery: 'parent' })`) but its description and result say the
child is already running, that nothing can observe it, and that the result arrives by itself.
## Progress and result delivery
An external child reports exactly once, when it settles: the harness injects a `Background subagent
<id> finished` notice with the child's closing message, and that notice starts the parent's next tur
n. There is no mid-run progress channel, and this is a property of the backend, not a bug in this pl
ere is no mid-run progress channel, and this is a property of the backend, not a bug in this plugin:
- the "task message" style notice (`Team message from <child>: …`) belongs to continuable **local**

children, which carry dsh's `send_message` tool and a parent inbox;
- a CodeBuddy child is a separat
e CLI process with no dsh tools, so it cannot call back into the parent's conversation, and the prov
ider advertises no `prepareContinuable`, so no inbox exists on either side.
What the tool can do — and does — is keep the parent from burning the run waiting: its result states
that polling is futile and that the parent should continue with other work or end its turn, which l
ets the settlement notice arrive at the earliest possible step boundary.
## The chat card: what it may claim
Each delegation also gets one card in the transcript (`conversation.chat.node`, kind `codebuddy-run`
), anchored on its own `tool/call` event. It folds exactly three things — the handoff result, the se
ttlement notice, and any mid-run message sent into it — because those are the only moments an extern
al child produces. That bounds what it can honestly say:
| State | Reached from | What the card shows |

| 运行中 | `tool/call` | the clock starts counting at the call |
| 后台运行中 | `tool/result` (the activatio
n notice) | the same clock, still counting; the body names the run and its log, and fills with the c

hild's actions as they arrive |
| 已完成 | settlement `finished` | the closing words, appended below th

e task and the timeline, with the CLI's cost line lifted into the header |
| 已停止 | settlement `was s

topped` | the notice kept whole — it is the only explanation there is |
| 被拒绝 | settlement `declined

the task` | idem |
| 失败 | settlement `failed before it finished` / `ended abnormally`, or a run tha
t raised | the diagnostic, plus any `- [done] …` steps |
**One run, one card.** A `codebuddy_steer` call is an ordinary tool call in the transcript, and it m
atches `/codebuddy/` just like the delegation does — so it would open a second card that nothing eve
r settles, sitting at 后台运行中 next to the run it only sent a message to. The definition therefore keys
on what a call *does*, not only on its name: a call whose arguments carry a `childId` addresses a r
un instead of starting one, and folds into the card that started that child (`↪ 插话 …` in its body),
or into nothing when this page never saw that card. Its own result is ignored either way — the run's
status changes only when the child settles. The ordinary tool row still reports the call.
[该节后续省略]
### Two records, each keeping what it alone knows
The CLI already writes a JSONL transcript per session (`~/.codebuddy/projects/<slug>/<sessionId>.jso
nl`): every call, its result, the reasoning between them, appended while the run is still going. Tha
t file is the best account of what the child did, so nothing tries to reproduce it — and the page re
st account of what the child did, so nothing tries to reproduce it — and the page reads it directly:
- **Timeline = transcript.** `bin/lib/timeline.mjs` folds calls and results on `callId` into coarse
rows, reading only the bytes appended since the last poll and keeping the newest 400. The card gets
the same information from ACP notifications over its own route, so a run reads the same in both plac

es; the transcript is the one that survives the host.
- **Log = what the provider alone witnessed.**
`~/.dsh/logs/subagent-codebuddy/<runId>.log` now records only events the CLI cannot: spawn, handsha
ke, session and transcript path, permission decisions, steer results, plan changes, *failed* tool ca
lls, stop reason, stderr. Copying every successful call into it made each run log ~250 KB of near-du
plicate lines — a one-hour run is now a few dozen lines, and it is the file that still exists when t
he transcript path is wrong or the CLI changed it.
That split is also why `-f` follows steps rather than lines: it prints one line per call as it start
s and again when it finishes, and only falls back to the log when a run has no transcript.
## Known Limitations and Deferred Work
- **One-shot, but steerable** — no durable continuable children and no follow-up turn after settleme

nt; each run is a fresh CLI process. While it runs, `codebuddy_steer` can still add a message.
- **A
uth is the machine's CLI login state** unless `envFile` supplies an API key or `authMethodId` select

s an advertised method.
- **Unattended approvals are auto-answered** (`permission: allow` by default
); no prompt is surfaced to a human. Use `permission: reject` for a child that must stay read-only.
